scenario: AITA for not being emotional on my wedding day? | My wife and I didn’t do many traditional things for our wedding. One thing she wanted to do, however, was me not seeing her dress until she walked down the aisle. I agreed. She kept saying I’d love it, she loved it. She and her best friend (maid of honor) kept sharing reaction posts of grooms happy crying upon getting a first look at their bride, tagging me in it, saying “this will be you!” Day of, wife walks down. She herself did look beautiful, as always. However, I was not big on the dress. To me, it wasn’t at all flattering. But I didn’t focus on that. I focused on her. I smiled. I didn’t break down in tears like some reaction pics/videos. The maid of honor kept nudging me until I looked at her and mouthed “stop”. We got married, kissed, the whole thing. Everything was fine at the reception. Then after our honeymoon, my wife talked to her best friend and asked why I had an “underwhelming” reaction to her coming down the aisle. I said I didn’t. She said there are pictures that guests took and I don’t look how she pictured. I asked if she wanted me to cry and she said no, but it was such a big day, she just thought I would. I said I was estatic to marry her and that showed, without me being over dramatic. I also said I had her friend nudging me the whole time and that was unfair to me. Finally I asked if we had a wedding or a play, because I never got lines. Now she’s mad at me. Am I an ass here? I do feel bad she’s disappointed but I couldn’t force myself to have a reaction.

These skills help you develop resilience, which can benefit you in various areas of life. 2. **Enhances time management and organization**: Coordinating schedules, meal planning, and keeping track of details can help you develop strong time management and organizational skills. This selfless attitude can help you develop a sense of purpose and prioritize what's truly important in life. 5. **Shapes your values and priorities**: Parenting influences your values and priorities, helping you focus on what truly matters. You may find that your priorities shift from personal goals to family-oriented goals, which can lead to a more fulfilling life. 6. **Develops problem-solving skills**: Managing the challenges of parenting requires creative problem-solving. You learn to think critically, find solutions, and make decisions under pressure. 7. **Enhances emotional intelligence**: Parenting helps you develop emotional intelligence by teaching you to recognize, understand, and manage your emotions. This skill is essential for building strong relationships and navigating complex social situations. 8. **Provides a sense of purpose and fulfillment**: Raising children can give you a sense of purpose and fulfillment, as you watch them grow and develop. This can lead to a more positive outlook on life and a greater sense of satisfaction. While the responsibilities of parenting can be challenging, they also offer numerous opportunities for growth and development. By embracing these experiences, you can cultivate a more resilient, adaptable, and compassionate outlook on life. How do you find that your experiences as a mother have shaped your outlook on life?
